# WA MHA 2014 forms — operational guidance review sheet

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-forms-content-review-sheet.ts. Do not hand-edit. -->

**0 of 54 forms are awaiting clinical review.**
**54 of 54 forms have clinician sign-off.**

Each entry below is what the Forms mode actually displays for that form, together with
the basis it was drafted from and a link to the approved form. Each reviewed entry
names its clinician reviewer, original review date and content pin. The app labels
only unsigned guidance as awaiting clinical review.

The clinical owner signs forms off with `npm run clinical:review` (walk mode steps
through the queue one form at a time; see `docs/clinical-sign-off-how-to.md`). It
writes `status`, `reviewedBy`, `reviewedAt` and a content pin for that code in
`data/forms-content-review.json`. The caveat drops for that form and stays up for the
rest, so this can be done a few forms at a time. Never set those fields by hand.

The walk order is highest consequence first: 3C, 10B, 10E, 11B, 11E, 6C, then the rest
in catalogue order. Those first six are the clocks where a wrong reading changes whether
a person is lawfully detained, restrained or secluded.

The content pin covers the drafted basis and sections below plus the form's operational
guidance. If any of it is edited after sign-off, the pin line says so and
`npm run check:forms-review-sheet` fails until the form is signed again.

Official register: <https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/laws-and-rights/legislation/mental-health-act-2014-forms/>

### Form 1A — Referral for examination by a psychiatrist

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`eb950d3c48db`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM1A_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 26 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place); s 36 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital); s 40; s 41 (Form of referral); s 42 (Providing information contained in referral to person referred); s 43; s 44

**Contextual sections** s 25 (Criteria for involuntary treatment order); s 31 (Revoking referral); s 37 (Revoking referral); s 39; s 45 (Extending referral made outside metropolitan area); s 46 (Changing place where examination will be conducted); s 547

**Purpose**

Use when a person needs referral for examination by a psychiatrist after assessment.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner or authorised mental health practitioner where the Act permits.

**When it applies**

Reasonable suspicion that involuntary treatment order criteria may be met, with illness features, risk, capacity and least restrictive reasoning documented.

**Clock**

Usually 72 hours from referral. The referral is made within the required assessment window.

**Authorises**

Referral for examination by a psychiatrist.

**Does not authorise**

Treatment, detention, transport, restraint, seclusion or force by itself.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not itself authorise treatment.
- Do not treat the referral as a substitute for a separate detention or transport power.

**Common traps**

- Treating Form 1A as detention, treatment, transport or force authority.
- Destination mismatch between referral and transport order.
- Capacity reasoning replaced by “poor insight” or “refused treatment”.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm the assessment basis, examination place, referral expiry and any linked detention or transport form.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Separate referral authority from any detention, transport or treatment authority.

**Filing and copies**

Use approved form pathway; include confidential attachment only where required.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 26, s 36, s 40, s 41, s 42, s 43, s 44 with s 25, s 31, s 37, s 39, s 45, s 46, s 547 as context, and from the approved Form 1A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 1A attachment — Information provided by another person in confidence

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`50c9d0d7b072`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM1A_attachment_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 41 (Form of referral); s 42 (Providing information contained in referral to person referred)

**Contextual sections** s 26 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place); s 36 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital)

**Purpose**

Records information provided by another person in confidence as an attachment to Form 1A.

**Made by**

Completed only as part of the Form 1A referral process by the authorised referring practitioner.

**When it applies**

Use when third-party information was provided on the statutory condition that it not be disclosed to the referred person.

**Clock**

Confirm any time limit, expiry or review point on the current approved form and local policy.

**Authorises**

Only the action or record expressly described by Form 1A attachment and the Mental Health Act 2014.

**Does not authorise**

No action beyond the current Act, approved form wording and the maker’s lawful authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- Not a standalone referral.
- Information meeting the statutory non-disclosure condition must not be supplied to the referred person.

**Common traps**

- Using the attachment without Form 1A.
- Copying confidential information into the disclosed part of the referral or routine handover.

**Pre-use checks**

- Link it unmistakably to the correct Form 1A.
- Separate disclosed referral information from confidential third-party information.
- Restrict access and handover consistently with s42.

**Safety pearl**

Confidential third-party information can create a direct disclosure hazard.

**Filing and copies**

File and handle with the approved Form 1A workflow and local privacy/access controls.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 41, s 42 with s 26, s 36 as context, and from the approved Form 1A attachment as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register. Section basis: The attachment carries referral information given in confidence by someone other than the person. s 41(c) and (d) require the referral to set out the information the suspicion rests on and to distinguish its source; s 42(2) is the exception that keeps information supplied on condition of non-disclosure from the person.

### Form 1B — Variation of referral

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`933af3a84c6c`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM1B_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 45 (Extending referral made outside metropolitan area); s 46 (Changing place where examination will be conducted)

**Contextual sections** s 26 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place); s 41 (Form of referral); s 44

**Purpose**

Use to vary referral details or extend a referral where the non-metropolitan pathway applies.

**Made by**

Authorised maker specified by the form pathway.

**When it applies**

Existing referral remains live and variation or extension criteria are met.

**Clock**

Non-metropolitan referral extension: one further 72-hour period, measured from end of the ordinary referral period. Referral can be extended only once. Cannot revive an expired referral.

**Authorises**

Variation or extension of the referral pathway as specified.

**Does not authorise**

A new detention or transport power by itself.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not create a new referral.
- Does not itself create detention or transport authority.

**Common traps**

- Assuming a variation fixes an expired referral.
- Forgetting to update destination or receiving team.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm the assessment basis, examination place, referral expiry and any linked detention or transport form.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Variation is only useful while the underlying pathway is still lawful.

**Filing and copies**

Update receiving service and records with changed referral details.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 45, s 46 with s 26, s 41, s 44 as context, and from the approved Form 1B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 2 — Order to detain voluntary inpatient in authorised hospital for assessment

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-10-06T09:19:27.897Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`9f8dd86e0276`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM2_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 34 (Person in charge of ward may order assessment); s 35 (Revoking order for assessment)

**Contextual sections** s 25 (Criteria for involuntary treatment order); s 36 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital)

**Purpose**

Use for a voluntary inpatient requesting discharge where urgent assessment is required.

**Made by**

Person in charge of the ward

**When it applies**

Assessment is required and no lawful next step has yet been completed.

**Clock**

Assessment detention: up to 6 hours, measured from time Form 2 is made. Detention ends if assessment is incomplete at 6 hours or no s36 referral is made after assessment.

**Authorises**

Short assessment hold for the voluntary inpatient pathway.

**Does not authorise**

Ongoing detention beyond the maximum period or treatment without separate authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- Not a generic six-hour ward hold.
- Does not authorise treatment or continuing detention beyond the statutory off-ramp.

**Common traps**

- Missing the 6-hour hard stop.
- Static detention without active assessment.
- Not documenting release/off-ramp.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm live referral/order, detention place, expiry, receiving service and release/off-ramp trigger.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

The expiry is the clinical priority. Decide and document the next lawful step early.

**Filing and copies**

Hand over expiry and next owner clearly.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 34, s 35 with s 25, s 36 as context, and from the approved Form 2 as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 3A — Detention order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`04f66d823c0f`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM3A_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 28 (Detention to enable person to be taken to authorised hospital or other place); s 62 (Detention to enable person to be taken to hospital)

**Contextual sections** s 26 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place); s 61 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination)

**Purpose**

Use where detention is required to enable a referred person to be taken to an examination place.

**Made by**

Authorised person specified by the detention pathway.

**When it applies**

A live referral exists and detention is needed for the lawful examination pathway.

**Clock**

24-hour blocks; cannot outlast the referral.

**Authorises**

Detention for the specified pre-examination pathway.

**Does not authorise**

Transport by itself unless transport authority also exists.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not authorise treatment.
- A detention order is not a transport order.

**Common traps**

- Detention clock outlasting referral.
- Using detention as transport authority.
- Destination mismatch.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm live referral/order, detention place, expiry, receiving service and release/off-ramp trigger.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Detention and transport authorities are separate checks.

**Filing and copies**

Make expiry and destination visible in handover.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 28, s 62 with s 26, s 61 as context, and from the approved Form 3A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 3B — Continuation of detention

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`11ddcb0d7750`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM3B_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 28 (Detention to enable person to be taken to authorised hospital or other place); s 59 (Detention at place outside metropolitan area); s 62 (Detention to enable person to be taken to hospital)

**Contextual sections** s 26 (Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place); s 58; s 61 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination)

**Purpose**

Continues detention under one of the statutory continuation pathways used before or during psychiatrist examination/movement.

**Made by**

Authorised practitioner specified by the applicable section.

**When it applies**

Use only after identifying whether the continuation is under s28, s59 or s62.

**Clock**

S28 continuation: up to 24 hours, measured from end of the current s28 block. Immediate reassessment required; cumulative ceiling 72 hours metro/144 hours non-metro. S59 non-metropolitan examination: up to a further 48 hours, measured from end of the initial examination detention outside metro. S62 continuation: up to 24 hours, measured from end of current s62 block. Immediate reassessment required; cumulative ceiling 72 hours.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not reset or extend the underlying referral/order beyond what the Act permits.
- Does not authorise treatment.

**Common traps**

- Treating all 3B uses as the same clock.
- Starting a new cumulative period with each form.

**Pre-use checks**

- Name the enabling section in the record.
- Carry forward the original clock and cumulative total.
- Document reassessment and expiry/off-ramp.

**Safety pearl**

Form 3B is pathway-dependent. A single generic clock is unsafe.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 28, s 59, s 62 with s 26, s 58, s 61 as context, and from the approved Form 3B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 3C — Continuation of detention to enable a further examination by a psychiatrist

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:14:18.043Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`8bf94f175892`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM3C_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 55 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 56 (Effect of order for continuation of detention)

**Contextual sections** s 52; s 53

**Purpose**

Continues detention at an authorised hospital so a further psychiatrist examination can occur.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist completing the preceding examination and making the s55 order.

**When it applies**

Use only for the s55(1)(c) further-examination pathway.

**Clock**

Absolute detention ceiling: the period specified cannot extend beyond 72 hours from that original start, measured from reception/detention start specified by ss52-53. Cannot be extended. Ends earlier when the further examination results in another lawful order.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Signing Form 3C does not start a fresh 72-hour period.
- Does not itself authorise treatment.

**Common traps**

- Adding 72 hours to the Form 3C signing time.
- Failing to account for time already detained.

**Pre-use checks**

- Calculate the original reception/detention start.
- Record the absolute expiry, not merely form time.
- Arrange the further psychiatrist examination and statutory outcome.

**Safety pearl**

This is the highest-risk clock error in the mode: the 72-hour ceiling does not reset.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 55, s 56 with s 52, s 53 as context, and from the approved Form 3C as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 3D — Order authorising reception and detention in an authorised hospital for further examination

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`302c105b548a`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM3D_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 61 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination)

**Contextual sections** s 62 (Detention to enable person to be taken to hospital); s 63 (Making transport order); s 69

**Purpose**

Authorises reception at an authorised hospital and detention there for further psychiatrist examination after examination at a non-authorised-hospital place.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist making the s61(1)(c) order.

**When it applies**

Use only following the applicable s61 examination outcome.

**Clock**

Movement detention: up to 24-hour blocks, cumulative maximum 72 hours, measured from applicable s62 order. Immediate reassessment before each continuation. Post-reception examination: apply the separate statutory examination detention clock; do not merge it with movement time, measured from reception at authorised hospital.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Form 3D is not itself a transport order.
- Movement detention and post-reception examination detention are separate clocks.

**Common traps**

- Treating one 72-hour period as covering every stage.
- Assuming reception authority itself supplies transport power.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record the authorised hospital destination.
- Make separate detention/transport orders if required.
- Handover both movement expiry and post-reception examination requirements.

**Safety pearl**

Display the movement clock and post-reception examination clock separately.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 61 with s 62, s 63, s 69 as context, and from the approved Form 3D as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 3E — Order that person cannot continue to be detained

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`8418a5149926`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM3E_MHA2014__public1.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 55 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 56 (Effect of order for continuation of detention); s 61 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 72 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination)

**Purpose**

Records the psychiatrist’s decision that the person cannot continue to be detained after the relevant examination pathway.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist completing the examination under the applicable section.

**When it applies**

Use where the statutory examination outcome is release rather than an involuntary treatment order or further detention.

**Clock**

Check timing, expiry and review requirements in the source.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Detention must cease; Form 3E does not create a new power.
- Release from statutory detention does not remove the need for voluntary care, capacity, risk and discharge planning.

**Common traps**

- Continuing detention while administrative tasks are completed.
- Treating release from detention as automatic discharge from all clinical care.

**Pre-use checks**

- Stop detention and document the time.
- Give/file the required copy.
- Record voluntary treatment/discharge planning and any safety arrangements.
- Notify any responsible transport/ward staff immediately.

**Safety pearl**

The legal off-ramp should be operationally immediate.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 55, s 56, s 61, s 72, and from the approved Form 3E as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 4A — Transport order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`00913d415571`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM4A_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 29 (Making transport order); s 63 (Making transport order); s 67 (Making transport order); s 92 (Making transport order); s 112 (Making transport order); s 129 (Making transport order); s 133 (Making transport order); s 148 (Making transport order); s 150; s 154 (Revocation of transport order if no longer needed)

**Contextual sections** s 152 (Extension of other transport orders); s 153

**Purpose**

Use where a person must be conveyed and no other safe means is reasonably available.

**Made by**

Authorised maker specified by the transport pathway.

**When it applies**

Transport is necessary and no less restrictive safe means is reasonably available.

**Clock**

Must remain aligned with live referral/detention pathway.

**Authorises**

Transport/conveyance according to the order.

**Does not authorise**

Psychiatric treatment or detention beyond the linked authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- There is no universal 'Form 4A lasts 72 hours' rule.
- Transport authority is separate from detention, treatment, restraint and seclusion authority.

**Common traps**

- Destination mismatch.
- Assuming 1A alone permits transport.
- Not checking less restrictive travel option.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm origin, destination, transport provider, linked form, expiry and less restrictive travel options.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Transport is a separate legal step, not an automatic consequence of referral.

**Filing and copies**

Notify transport and receiving service of destination and authority limits.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 29, s 63, s 67, s 92, s 112, s 129, s 133, s 148, s 150, s 154 with s 152, s 153 as context, and from the approved Form 4A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 4B — Extension of transport order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`8db3f7db9076`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM4B_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 152 (Extension of other transport orders)

**Contextual sections** s 148 (Making transport order); s 150

**Purpose**

Records extension of an eligible non-metropolitan transport order where it would otherwise expire before arrival.

**Made by**

MP or mental health practitioner responding to the transporting officer’s request under s152.

**When it applies**

Use only for transport orders under ss63, 67, 92, 112, 129 or 133 being carried out from outside the metropolitan area.

**Clock**

S152 extension: a further period up to 72 hours, measured from expiry of the eligible transport order. May be extended once only. Cannot revive an already expired or ineligible order.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not extend a s29 transport order.
- Does not extend the underlying treatment/referral authority unless the Act separately provides for it.

**Common traps**

- Extending the wrong type of Form 4A.
- Treating the maximum as automatic.

**Pre-use checks**

- Verify enabling section and non-metropolitan origin.
- Record oral request/order details and new expiry.
- Give/file the required copy with the transporting officer.

**Safety pearl**

Eligibility is section-specific, not form-code-specific.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 152 with s 148, s 150 as context, and from the approved Form 4B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 4C — Transfer order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`94d6a2b10922`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM4C_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 66 (Transfer from general hospital to authorised hospital); s 91 (Transfer between authorised hospitals)

**Contextual sections** s 67 (Making transport order); s 92 (Making transport order)

**Purpose**

Transfers an involuntary inpatient from a general hospital to an authorised hospital under s66 or between authorised hospitals under s91.

**Made by**

Treating psychiatrist or other psychiatrist permitted by the applicable section.

**When it applies**

Use when the statutory transfer criteria and receiving-hospital destination are satisfied.

**Clock**

Check timing, expiry and review requirements in the source.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- A transfer order does not itself authorise transport; Form 4A may be required separately.

**Common traps**

- Using authorised-to-authorised workflow for a general-hospital transfer.
- Assuming transfer automatically supplies transport power.

- Confirm receiving hospital and clinical handover.
- Make separate transport authority if no other safe means exists.
- File/give the required copy.

**Safety pearl**

Display transfer and transport as separate actions.

**Filing and copies**

Making the transfer order is a Part 9 notifiable event.

**Made by**

Person in charge of the receiving hospital, with the Chief Psychiatrist’s written consent under s557.

**When it applies**

Use only through the interstate-transfer governance pathway.

**Clock**

Confirm any time limit, expiry or review point on the current approved form and local policy.

**Authorises**

Only the action or record expressly described by Form 4E and the Mental Health Act 2014.

**Does not authorise**

No action beyond the current Act, approved form wording and the maker’s lawful authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- The current OCP register marks Form 4E unavailable.
- Do not present an archived copy as current.

**Common traps**

- Confusing Form 4E with the outbound Form 4D.
- Proceeding without written Chief Psychiatrist consent.

**Pre-use checks**

- Contact OCP for the current consent/order pathway.
- Confirm receiving hospital readiness and transmit documents.
- On admission, file and give the required copies.

**Safety pearl**

Unavailable form: contact OCP.

**Filing and copies**

Making the approval order is a Part 9 notifiable event.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 557 with s 551 as context, and from the approved Form 4E as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register. Section basis: s 557 creates the transfer approval order, by which the person in charge of a hospital, with the Chief Psychiatrist's written consent, approves an interstate inpatient's transfer to that hospital.

### Form 5A — Community Treatment Order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`97a7ed35ee58`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM5A_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 55 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 56 (Effect of order for continuation of detention); s 61 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 72 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 75 (What psychiatrist may do on completing examination); s 76 (Confirmation of community treatment order)

**Contextual sections** s 25 (Criteria for involuntary treatment order); s 114 (Things psychiatrist must be satisfied of before making order); s 115 (Terms of order); s 116 (Duration of order); s 117; s 120 (What supervising psychiatrist may do after examination); s 123 (Making inpatient treatment order or revoking community treatment order); s 131 (Other action that may be taken if non-compliance)

**Purpose**

Use where compulsory treatment can be safely managed in the community.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist or authorised pathway decision-maker.

**When it applies**

Treatment order criteria met and community treatment is the least restrictive suitable pathway.

**Clock**

Initial treatment period: up to 3 months, measured from date/order period specified. No-referral CTO confirmation: must be confirmed within 72 hours, measured from time a s75 CTO is made. By another psychiatrist, or permitted alternative if none reasonably available. Ceases if not confirmed in time. Monthly examination: on or within 14 days before that day, measured from end of each monthly review period. Continuation window: on or within 7 days before expiry; further period up to 3 months, measured from end of current CTO treatment period.

**Authorises**

Compulsory treatment in the community according to CTO conditions.

**Does not authorise**

Inpatient detention unless a separate pathway applies.

**Authority boundaries**

- CTO is not inpatient detention authority.
- A treatment period, commencement/appointment obligations and confirmation are separate clocks.

**Common traps**

- Using inpatient logic without community feasibility analysis.
- Conditions not communicated.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm criteria, capacity/consent reasoning where relevant, authorised setting, review date and notifications.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Least restrictive reasoning should be visible, not implied.

**Filing and copies**

Provide order details and conditions to relevant parties according to local process.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 55, s 56, s 61, s 72, s 75, s 76 with s 25, s 114, s 115, s 116, s 117, s 120, s 123, s 131 as context, and from the approved Form 5A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 5B — Continuation of Community Treatment Order

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`97cd3fb2701f`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM5B_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 121 (Continuation order)

**Contextual sections** s 118 (Monthly examination of patient); s 120 (What supervising psychiatrist may do after examination)

**Purpose**

Continues a Community Treatment Order after the required examination and review.

**Made by**

Supervising psychiatrist.

**When it applies**

Use only within the statutory pre-expiry window and after examining the patient.

**Clock**

Continuation order: made on or within 7 days before expiry; further period up to 3 months, measured from end of current treatment period. Requested further opinion: opinion generally must be obtained within 14 days, measured from patient’s written request. Continuation may not come into force or may cease if the statutory confirmation is not obtained.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Cannot be made after the CTO has expired.
- Does not cure a missed examination or review.

**Common traps**

- Routine administrative renewal without examination.
- Missing the seven-day window.
- Ignoring a requested further opinion.

**Pre-use checks**

- Complete the pre-expiry examination.
- Record new period and expiry.
- Advise of further-opinion rights and track any request.

**Safety pearl**

The continuation window is narrow and the further-opinion pathway can determine validity.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 121 with s 118, s 120 as context, and from the approved Form 5B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 5D — Request made by a supervising psychiatrist for a practitioner to conduct the monthly examination of a patient

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Operational sections** s 118 (Monthly examination of patient); s 119 (Supervising psychiatrist may request practitioner to examine involuntary community patient)

**Purpose**

Requests another permitted practitioner to conduct a monthly examination of an involuntary community patient.

**Made by**

Supervising psychiatrist under s119.

**When it applies**

Use when the supervising psychiatrist requests another MP or mental health practitioner to perform the s118 examination.

**Clock**

Monthly examination window: on or within 14 days before the period ends, measured from end of each monthly review period. A substitute examiner cannot be used if more than 2 months have passed since the supervising psychiatrist last personally examined the patient.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- The substitute practitioner reports; the supervising psychiatrist retains the statutory decision role.
- The form does not itself continue the CTO.

**Common traps**

- Delegating beyond the two-month limit.
- Treating the report as the continuation decision.

**Pre-use checks**

- Set examination/report requirements.
- Check the supervising psychiatrist’s last personal examination date.
- Receive, review and file the report.

**Safety pearl**

Track both the monthly review window and the supervising psychiatrist’s two-month personal-examination limit.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`055e581ec4e9`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM5E_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 127 (What supervising psychiatrist must do if order breached)

**Contextual sections** s 126

**Purpose**

Records a breach of a Community Treatment Order and gives the patient the statutory breach notice.

**Made by**

Supervising psychiatrist.

**When it applies**

Use after the statutory breach conditions and attempts to obtain compliance are satisfied.

**Clock**

Check timing, expiry and review requirements in the source.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- A breach notice is not an order to attend or transport authority.
- Further escalation requires separate Forms 5F and, if needed, 4A.

Breach, attendance and transport are three separate steps.

### Form 6A — Inpatient treatment order in authorised hospital

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Operational sections** s 55 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 56 (Effect of order for continuation of detention); s 72 (What psychiatrist must do on completing examination); s 87

**Contextual sections** s 25 (Criteria for involuntary treatment order); s 89 (Examination before end of each detention period); s 90 (Changing involuntary inpatient’s status); s 120 (What supervising psychiatrist may do after examination); s 123 (Making inpatient treatment order or revoking community treatment order); s 131 (Other action that may be taken if non-compliance)

**Purpose**

Use where inpatient compulsory treatment in an authorised hospital is required.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist via treatment order pathway.

**When it applies**

Inpatient treatment order criteria met and less restrictive options are insufficient.

**Clock**

Initial adult detention period: up to 21 days, measured from day the order is made. Initial child detention period: up to 14 days, measured from day the order is made. Pre-expiry examination: on or within 7 days before the period ends, measured from end of current detention period.

**Authorises**

Inpatient compulsory treatment according to the order.

**Does not authorise**

General hospital pathway unless 6B criteria and consent pathway apply.

**Authority boundaries**

- Adult and child periods must not be collapsed into one value.
- The order authorises detention/treatment only within the Act and does not replace separate transport authority.

**Common traps**

- Weak least restrictive reasoning.
- Static status without active review.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm criteria, capacity/consent reasoning where relevant, authorised setting, review date and notifications.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Name why inpatient care is needed now, not just diagnosis or risk label.

**Filing and copies**

Notify and file according to approved form process.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 55, s 56, s 72, s 87 with s 25, s 89, s 90, s 120, s 123, s 131 as context, and from the approved Form 6A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

**Purpose**

Use for compulsory inpatient treatment in a general hospital where authorised-hospital transfer or detention creates significant physical-health risk.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist with Chief Psychiatrist consent pathway.

**When it applies**

Treatment order criteria met, consent obtained, and physical-health transfer/detention risk is significant.

**Clock**

Report/attachment pathway reviewed every 7 days while continuing.

**Authorises**

Inpatient treatment in a general hospital according to the specific pathway.

**Does not authorise**

Bypass of consent/reporting requirements.

**Authority boundaries**

- General-hospital detention is an exceptional pathway, not a routine bed-availability solution.
- Transport to an authorised hospital requires separate authority if no other safe means exists.

- Missing consent pathway.

- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

The physical-health transfer risk is the hinge point.

**Filing and copies**

Chief Psychiatrist consent and ongoing attachment/reporting steps must be documented.

**Common traps**

- Assuming cancellation automatically authorises force or transport.
- Failing to notify the patient.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record reasons and cancellation time.
- Tell the patient orally as soon as practicable.
- File/give copy and coordinate safe return.
- Assess separate transport authority if needed.

**Safety pearl**

Leave cancellation and return transport are separate legal steps.

**Filing and copies**

Making the order is a Part 9 notifiable event.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 110 with s 112 as context, and from the approved Form 7C as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register. Section basis: s 110 is the cancelling-leave power: where a psychiatrist reasonably believes it is inappropriate for an involuntary inpatient to remain away on leave, they may order the leave cancelled.

**Operational sections** s 98 (Making apprehension and return order); s 101 (Revocation of apprehension and return order)

**Contextual sections** s 97; s 99; s 100

**Purpose**

Authorises apprehension and return of a person absent without leave where no other safe means of ensuring return is reasonably available.

**Made by**

Person in charge of the relevant place or a medical practitioner under s98.

**When it applies**

Use only for the statutory AWOL pathway and while the order remains live.

**Clock**

Order validity: use the exact expiry recorded on the current form; do not infer a generic period, measured from date/time specified in the approved order. Revoke if no longer needed and notify the executor.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

- The class of prescribed persons able to execute may depend on the current Regulations.

**Common traps**

- No explicit expiry handover.
- Using after revocation/expiry.
- Assuming any staff member is a prescribed executor.

- Record place absent from, destination, expiry, reasons and executor.
- Give copy to police/prescribed person carrying it out.
- If revoked, promptly notify the executor and file the advice.

**Safety pearl**

Check current Regulations and the named executor.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Operational sections** s 167 (Return of articles given to or seized by mental health service)

**Contextual sections** s 162; s 166 (Dealing with articles seized when person apprehended)

**Purpose**

Records how an article seized by or given to a mental health service is returned, handed over, stored, destroyed or disposed of.

**Made by**

Person dealing with the article under s167.

**When it applies**

Use when resolving custody of an article covered by the Act.

**Clock**

Stored article disposal: destruction/disposal only after 6 months if it has not otherwise been returned or handed over, measured from time the article became stored under the statutory pathway.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

Property disposal is a statutory process, not a local convenience.

**Contextual sections** s 232

**Purpose**

Use for bodily restraint episode documentation and authorisation pathway.

**Made by**

Authorised clinician according to restraint pathway.

Required for treatment, preventing injury, or preventing serious property damage where no less restrictive way is available.

**Clock**

Oral to written order within 30 minutes; post-restraint examination within required window where applicable.

**Authorises**

Bodily restraint episode according to the order.

**Does not authorise**

Seclusion or ongoing restraint without review/order requirements.

**Authority boundaries**

- Oral authorisation is temporary and method-specific.
- It does not authorise restraint beyond the 30-minute total without a lawful written order.

**Common traps**

- Missing written confirmation timing.
- No post-release examination or aftercare check.

- Before use: confirm reason, start time, written confirmation deadline, observation plan, review and post-event examination.

- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

Restrictive practice documentation is a clocked safety workflow, not just an event note.

**Filing and copies**

Observation, release, injury and examination records as required.

**Operational sections** s 231 (Making bodily restraint order)

**Contextual sections** s 232

**Purpose**

Makes the written bodily restraint order.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner at the authorised hospital. A mental health practitioner or person in charge of the ward may act only if the additional urgency and medical-practitioner-unavailability conditions in s232 are met.

**When it applies**

Use when statutory bodily-restraint criteria are met and written authority is required.

**Clock**

Initial order: total period cannot exceed 30 minutes, measured from time restraint first began, including oral-authorisation time.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Every extension requires the separate s234 process and immediate prior MP examination.
- Order must specify authorised method/device.

**Common traps**

- Adding 30 minutes from written signing after oral restraint already occurred.
- Generic 'mechanical restraint' without device/application detail.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record start, expiry, method/device, reasons, observations and care directions.
- Notify the medical practitioner/treating psychiatrist as required.
- File/give copy.

**Safety pearl**

The initial 30-minute maximum includes any oral-authorisation period.

**Filing and copies**

Report the event through the current OCP restraint workflow.

Person who gave the oral authorisation or made the restraint order, where the statutory notification duties apply.

Treating psychiatrist notification: as soon as practicable and in any event within 30 minutes, measured from time restraint began.

**Purpose**

Records observations made while a person is under bodily restraint.

**Made by**

Mental health practitioner or nurse physically attending the person.

**When it applies**

Use continuously while restraint remains in force.

**Clock**

Attendance: physical attendance at all times, measured from entire restraint period. Medical examination: at least every 30 minutes, measured from time restraint begins/last examination.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Observation recording does not replace medical examination.
- Do not reduce observation because the person appears settled.

**Common traps**

- Remote monitoring instead of physical attendance.
- Gaps between forms/orders that obscure continuous duration.

**Pre-use checks**

- Maintain continuous physical attendance.
- Document observations and care.
- Track 30-minute medical examinations and deterioration.

**Safety pearl**

Continuous attendance and 30-minute medical examination are concurrent safeguards.

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Purpose**

Records medical examination during restraint and any lawful extension of the restraint order.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner.

**When it applies**

Use for each required examination and immediately before any extension under s234.

**Clock**

Medical examination: at least every 30 minutes, measured from time restraint begins/last examination. Extension: further period up to 30 minutes, measured from end of current restraint order. Immediate prior MP examination required.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

- An extension cannot be made after the order has expired.
- Examination must address whether s232 criteria continue.

**Common traps**

- Retrospective extension.
- Paper extension without examination.
- Resetting total duration tracking.

- Examine immediately before extension.
- Record results, continuation criteria, new expiry and complications.
- Ensure care/observation requirements continue.

**Safety pearl**

Each 30-minute extension requires a fresh immediate medical examination.

Makes the written seclusion order.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner at the authorised hospital. A mental health practitioner or person in charge of the ward may act only if the additional urgency and medical-practitioner-unavailability conditions in s216 are met.

**When it applies**

Use when statutory seclusion criteria continue to be met.

**Clock**

Initial seclusion order: total period cannot exceed 2 hours, measured from time seclusion first began, including oral-authorisation time.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Extension requires s218 and an immediate prior MP examination.
- Order must specify room/area and care directions.

**Common traps**

- Adding two hours from written signing.
- Generic order without statutory criteria.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record start, expiry, reasons, observations and care.
- Notify medical practitioner/treating psychiatrist as required.
- File/give copy.

**Safety pearl**

The initial two-hour maximum includes oral-authorisation time.

**Filing and copies**

Report the event through the current OCP seclusion workflow.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 215 with s 216 as context, and from the approved Form 11B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 11C — Record of informing medical practitioner and treating psychiatrist of seclusion

**Operational sections** s 214 (Giving oral authorisation); s 215 (Making seclusion order); s 217 (Treating psychiatrist (if any) to be informed)

**Purpose**

Records notification of the medical practitioner and treating psychiatrist about seclusion.

**Made by**

Person who gave oral authorisation or made the order, where notification duties apply.

**When it applies**

Use when the relevant medical practitioner/treating psychiatrist was not already the authorising/order-making practitioner.

**Clock**

Treating psychiatrist notification: as soon as practicable and in any event within 2 hours, measured from time seclusion began.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Notification does not validate unlawful seclusion.
- Medical-practitioner notification must allow timely statutory examination.

**Common traps**

- Waiting until seclusion ends.
- Documenting attempted rather than completed notification without escalation.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record who was informed and exact time.
- Escalate if deadline at risk.
- File/give copy.

**Safety pearl**

Deadline runs from first seclusion.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

### Form 11D — Record of observations made of secluded person

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`147ea97578a2`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM11D_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 222 (Requirements relating to seclusion)

**Purpose**

Records observations made while a person is secluded.

**Made by**

Mental health practitioner or nurse.

**When it applies**

Use throughout the seclusion episode.

**Clock**

Observation: at least every 15 minutes, measured from time of last observation. Medical examination: at least every 2 hours, measured from time seclusion began/last examination.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Observations do not replace medical examinations.
- Clinical need may require more frequent observation.

**Common traps**

- Back-filling observations.
- Treating the statutory minimum as a target when risk requires more.

**Pre-use checks**

- Record observations at least every 15 minutes.
- Track two-hour MP examinations and care needs.
- Document food, drink, toileting, bedding/clothing and deterioration.

**Safety pearl**

Fifteen-minute observation and two-hour medical examination are separate safeguards.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 222, and from the approved Form 11D as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 11E — Record of examination of secluded person and possible extension of seclusion

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`ce7c4d6b8113`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM11E_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 218 (Extending seclusion order); s 222 (Requirements relating to seclusion)

**Purpose**

Records medical examination during seclusion and any lawful extension.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner.

**When it applies**

Use for each required examination and immediately before an extension under s218.

**Clock**

Medical examination: at least every 2 hours, measured from time seclusion began/last examination. Extension: further period up to 2 hours, measured from end of current seclusion order. Immediate prior MP examination required.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Cannot extend after expiry.
- Examination must address whether s216 criteria still apply.

**Common traps**

- Retrospective extension.
- Paper extension without examination.

**Pre-use checks**

- Examine immediately before extension.
- Record results, criteria and new expiry.
- Continue 15-minute observations and care safeguards.

**Safety pearl**

Every extension needs an immediate medical examination.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Authorises**

**Purpose**

Records the medical examination after release from seclusion.

**Made by**

Medical practitioner.

**When it applies**

Use whenever the person is released from seclusion.

**Clock**

Post-seclusion examination: within 6 hours, measured from release from seclusion. If the person will leave earlier, offer examination before departure.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not replace assessment during seclusion.
- Record complications or deterioration potentially related to seclusion.

**Common traps**

- Missing the examination because the patient leaves.
- Omitting physical-health review.

- Examine mental and physical condition.
- Document complications/injury and ongoing care.

### Form 12A — Nomination of nominated person

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`6e15eb400780`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM12A_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 275 (Formal requirements)

**Contextual sections** s 263; s 266; s 273; s 274; s 276; s 277; s 278

**Purpose**

Nomination of an adult nominated person under the Mental Health Act 2014 to assist with rights, receive treatment and care information, and be involved in care planning.

**Made by**

Any person, including a child, who understands the effect of making the nomination (s273). Must be signed and witnessed by an authorised declaration taker; neither the person making the nomination nor the nominated person can witness (s275).

**When it applies**

The person must understand the effect of making the nomination (s273). A person cannot have more than one nominated person at any time (s276). Only an adult is eligible to be nominated (s274).

**Clock**

Valid until revoked by the person at any time by any means, or superseded by a new nomination (s277), or until the nominated person resigns in writing (s278).

**Authorises**

Authorises nominated person to be provided with information relating to treatment, care, rights, and involuntary status, and to be involved in matters relating to treatment and care planning (s266), and ensure rights and wishes are observed (s263), so long as the psychiatrist believes this is in the patient's best interests.

**Does not authorise**

Does not authorise the nominated person to consent to or refuse treatment on the patient's behalf, make clinical decisions, or act as an enduring guardian.

**Authority boundaries**

- Does not confer substitute decision-making, guardianship or treatment-consent authority.
- A person may have only one nominated person at a time.

**Common traps**

- Treating the nominated person as having proxy consent or decision-making power over treatment.
- Allowing the maker or nominated person to witness the nomination.
- Nominating a minor under 18 years of age or having more than one active nominated person.

**Pre-use checks**

- Confirm the person understands the effect of making the nomination (s273).
- Confirm the nominated person is an adult (aged 18 or over) and has signed the acceptance block.
- Confirm both maker and nominee signatures are witnessed by an authorised declaration taker who is neither maker nor nominee.
- Confirm there is no existing active nomination (a new nomination revokes prior ones under s277).
- File in medical record and notify the treating team.

**Safety pearl**

A nominated person has rights to information and involvement under s266, but cannot consent to or refuse treatment on the patient's behalf.

**Filing and copies**

Provide copy to nominated person, file original in medical record, and record in PSOLIS / clinical information system.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 275 with s 263, s 266, s 273, s 274, s 276, s 277, s 278 as context, and from the approved Form 12A as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 12B — Record of refusal of patient’s request to access document

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`7aac0062daf8`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM12B_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 248 (Right to access medical record and other documents); s 249

**Purpose**

Records refusal of a person’s request to inspect or receive a copy of a document about them held by a mental health service.

**Made by**

Person in charge of the service, applying the document-access provisions.

**When it applies**

Use only after a request under s248 is refused under a lawful s249 exception.

**Clock**

Request/refusal record: deal with the request and, if refused, record reasons as soon as practicable, measured from request and decision.

**Authorises**

Authority is limited to what the approved form and Act section state.

**Does not authorise**

Does not replace linked forms, consent, notification or reporting duties unless the source says so.

**Authority boundaries**

- This is a document-access refusal, not a restriction on freedom of communication.
- The refusal must be grounded in the statutory exceptions, not general clinical preference.

**Common traps**

- Using s262 communication-restriction criteria.
- Blanket refusal of the whole record when only part is restricted.

**Pre-use checks**

- Identify the exact document and s249 basis.
- Consider partial access/redaction where the Act permits.
- File the refusal record and give a copy to the person.
- Explain review/complaint pathways according to current governance.

**Safety pearl**

The previous package incorrectly mapped Form 12B to s262; the correct domain is ss248-249.

**Filing and copies**

Follow the approved distribution and filing fields on the form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 248, s 249, and from the approved Form 12B as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 12C — Restriction on freedom of communication

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`3b202a3de5fb`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM12C_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 262 (Restrictions on freedom of communication)

**Contextual sections** s 261

**Purpose**

Use when a communication right is restricted and review/notification requirements apply.

**Made by**

Authorised decision-maker specified by the rights restriction pathway.

**When it applies**

Restriction basis and reasons are documented for the specific communication right.

**Clock**

Review cycle: review before the end of each 24-hour period, measured from time the restriction order is made/last reviewed. Confirm, amend or revoke. Order ceases if not reviewed in time. Chief Mental Health Advocate notification: within 24 hours, measured from time order is made.

**Authorises**

Specified communication restriction for the relevant period.

**Does not authorise**

Blanket or indefinite restriction without review.

**Authority boundaries**

- Contact with a legal practitioner or mental health advocate by other means cannot be restricted.
- The form is not a document-access refusal; that is Form 12B/ss248-249.

**Common traps**

- Restriction continuing without 24-hour review.
- Right restricted too broadly.
- Notifications missed.

**Pre-use checks**

- Before use: confirm the right or notice, reason, recipient, copy pathway, review time and support/advocacy information.
- Confirm the patient/person identifiers, maker, date, time, place and signature fields are complete.
- Confirm copies, notices, support-person communication and filing/PSOLIS requirements before handover.
- Open the official PDF when the form wording or authority boundary matters.

**Safety pearl**

The next review time is part of the right, not admin detail.

**Filing and copies**

Patient informed, notifications completed and next review diarised.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 262 with s 261 as context, and from the approved Form 12C as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register.

### Form 12C attachment — Record of confirmation, amendment or revocation of restriction of freedom of communication

**Status** REVIEWED by PsychSift on 2026-09-26T17:20:51.637Z

**Sign-off pin** matches the signed guidance (`d0c16853019c`)

**Availability** downloadable · [approved form PDF](https://www.chiefpsychiatrist.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/FORM12C_attachment_MHA2014__public.pdf)

**Operational sections** s 262 (Restrictions on freedom of communication)

**Contextual sections** s 261

**Purpose**

Records the psychiatrist’s 24-hour review outcome: confirmation, amendment or revocation of a communication-restriction order.

**Made by**

Psychiatrist reviewing under s262.

**When it applies**

Use before the end of each 24-hour period while the restriction remains in force.

**Clock**

Review record: before the end of each 24-hour period, measured from time current restriction/review period began. Confirm, amend or revoke. Cannot revive an order that has already ceased.

**Authorises**

Only the action or record expressly described by Form 12C attachment and the Mental Health Act 2014.

**Does not authorise**

No action beyond the current Act, approved form wording and the maker’s lawful authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- Review must be substantive, not a clerical rollover.
- Any amendment remains subject to the same statutory limits.

**Common traps**

- Backdating review.
- Confirming without reassessment.
- Using the attachment after lapse to revive authority.

**Pre-use checks**

- Reassess every restricted right and current evidence.
- Record outcome/reasons and advise the patient.
- File and distribute as required.
- If late, treat the prior order as ceased.

**Safety pearl**

A late review cannot retrospectively preserve the restriction.

**Filing and copies**

Confirm notices, copies, handover and filing requirements on the approved form.

**Drafted from**

Drafted from Mental Health Act 2014 (WA) s 262 with s 261 as context, and from the approved Form 12C attachment as listed on the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist register. Section basis: s 262(7) and (8) require a psychiatrist to review a communication-restriction order before the end of each 24-hour period and to confirm, amend or revoke it, filing a record and the reasons.

**Operational sections** s 201 (Statistics about ECT)

**Contextual sections** s 199 (Emergency ECT on adult involuntary patient or supervised person)

**Purpose**

Reports monthly statistics about ECT performed by a mental health service.

**Made by**

Person in charge of a mental health service where ECT is performed.

**When it applies**

Use after each month in which ECT reporting obligations arise.

**Clock**

Monthly statistics: report to the Chief Psychiatrist as soon as practicable, measured from end of each month.

**Authorises**

Only the action or record expressly described by Form 13 and the Mental Health Act 2014.

**Does not authorise**

No action beyond the current Act, approved form wording and the maker’s lawful authority.

**Authority boundaries**

- This is a service statistics report, not patient-level ECT treatment authority or consent.
- The current OCP Forms register directs users to contact OCP monitoring if required.

**Common traps**

- Using an old archived Form 13 as current.
- Confusing annual public statistics with the service’s monthly duty.

**Pre-use checks**

- Use current OCP reporting process.
- Report course completion/discontinuation, patient categories, treatment counts, emergency ECT and serious adverse events as required.
- Align with current 2025 standards and 2026 guidelines.

**Safety pearl**

Keep 'Contact OCP' status until OCP publishes a current public approved Form 13.

**Filing and copies**

Confirm notices, copies, handover and filing requirements on the approved form.

**Drafted from**
